item.title: Akiyoshido Cave: Japan's Largest Limestone Cavern — Guide
item.description: Akiyoshido is the largest limestone cave in Japan and one of the longest in East Asia, carved over hundreds of thousands of years beneath the Akiyoshidai plateau in central Yamaguchi. A well-lit walking route of about a kilometre leads through a cool, cavernous underground world: soaring chambers, an underground river, and remarkable formations including the ‘Hundred Plates’, a hillside of terraced limestone pools, and towering columns and draperies. The cave holds a steady temperature around 17°C year-round, making it refreshing in summer and mild in winter.

item.title: Enzan Limestone Cave, Tara — Guide
item.description: Enzan Limestone Cave, in the Tara area of southern Saga, is a small limestone cave offering a cool, quiet underground experience away from the crowds. Formed over long ages as water dissolved the limestone rock, its passages hold stalactites, flowstone and cave formations, lit for visitors to explore on foot. Caves like this stay at a steady cool temperature year-round, making them refreshing on a hot summer day, and offer a glimpse of the slow geological processes shaping the mountains.

item.title: Ryugado Cave: Kochi's Limestone Wonder — Guide
item.description: Ryugado is counted among Japan’s three great limestone caves, a spectacular cavern carved over a million and a half years into the hills of eastern Kochi. A well-lit walking route of around a kilometre leads through soaring chambers past a wealth of formations — stalactites, flowstone curtains, an underground waterfall and pools — with the added fascination of ancient traces showing that people lived at the cave mouth some two thousand years ago.

item.title: Ryusendo Cave: Iwate's Cobalt Underground Lakes — Guide
item.description: Ryusendo is one of Japan’s three great limestone caves. Its underground lakes glow an impossibly vivid cobalt blue under the lights, with water clarity measured at over 40 metres — among the world’s clearest. A 700-metre illuminated walking route passes stalactites, underground rivers and silent crystal pools. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Iwaizumi, Iwate Hours ~8:30–17:00 (seasonal) Admission Around ¥1,100 Time needed About 1 hour Best time Year-round (10°C inside) What to See Underground lakes glowing cobalt blue with 40 m+ clarity.
